body:
`get_locale()` (cps/cw_babel.py:53-56) returns `current_user.locale` verbatim for
any logged-in non-Guest user. The value is not constrained to the locales we ship.

Validation on the write side is inconsistent:

- `cps/admin.py:947` DOES validate: `if vals['value'] in get_available_translations()`.
- `cps/web.py:2908` does NOT: `current_user.locale = to_save.get("locale", "en")`.
  This is the self-service profile route, so any authenticated user can store an
  arbitrary string as their own locale.
- `cps/admin.py:2888` and `cps/admin.py:3148` also assign without validation.

The `?lang=` per-request override IS validated (`_coerce_locale` against
available), so the stored-locale path is the gap.

Impact found so far: the value flowed into a filesystem path segment in
`render_template.translations_missing_notification`, where `'../../..'` resolved
to `cps/LC_MESSAGES` — outside the translations tree. Fixed at that callsite in
PR #1449 with a containment assertion, but the callsite is the symptom. Other
consumers of `get_locale()` inherit the same untrusted value, and each one has to
remember to defend itself.

The root fix is to validate on write in `web.py:2908` (and the two admin
assignments) against `get_available_translations()`, matching what
`admin.py:947` already does, so `get_locale()` can be trusted by its callers.

Authenticated-only and low reach on its own; filed rather than shipped because
the write-side fix touches three routes and wants its own change.

Not user-reported. Surfaced while fixing #1447.
title: user.locale is stored unvalidated and reaches get_locale() verbatim

resolution.note: Fixed by moving the boundary to the READ path, after an adversarial review returned MERGE-BLOCKER on the first attempt. That first attempt validated four classic-UI write sites and claimed to close this; it did not. Three SPA writers were untouched - POST /api/v1/account/profile, and the SPA admin create and update endpoints - so the primary modern surface remained directly exploitable by any authenticated user, while four mutation tests went green because every mutant was in a file the fix had already changed. What actually closes it: get_locale() now coerces the STORED locale against the available set, not just the ?lang= override. Write validation can only ever cover writers someone remembered; read-time coercion additionally covers (a) rows written before validation existed, (b) an unvalidated config_default_locale copied into new accounts by public registration, LDAP import and auto-creation, generic OAuth, and reverse-proxy provisioning, and (c) any writer added later. An unusable stored value falls through to Accept-Language negotiation rather than being returned - the case that matters is a user whose bad locale breaks their own profile page, who could never reach a write-side fix. Write-side validation is retained as hygiene and now covers all SEVEN assignment sites: cps/web.py profile, cps/admin.py _handle_new_user / user editor / ajax field editor, and cps/api/account.py + cps/api/admin.py (x2). CORRECTION to an earlier version of this note: it claimed each SPA site had been reverted as a mutant and gone red. That was not reproducible for admin_create_user - the mutant run had exercised the SPA EDIT site, never the CREATE site, and a full revert of the create site stayed green across the entire suite. A second cross-family review found it. The guard is now an ast walk over every `<anything>.locale = ...` assignment rather than a line regex over a hand-listed three names, and the config-default exemption matches a prefix rather than a substring; the exact revert now fails. _coerce_locale also gained a non-string guard: SPA writers hand it raw JSON, where 123 or {} would have hit .replace() and 500ed the request. Red/green: 31 tests, red on the parent, green after. Mutation-tested: read path returning the stored value verbatim, each SPA site reverted, and the non-string guard removed - all red. The test guard's module list was enumerated with a repo-wide grep rather than taken from the diff, because scoping it to changed files is exactly how the SPA writers were missed the first time. STILL OPEN, deliberately, and worth its own change: config_default_locale itself is stored unvalidated by both the classic and SPA configuration endpoints. Read-time coercion means it can no longer break locale resolution, but the database still cannot be assumed to hold only shipped locales. SECOND REVIEW (of the shipped architecture, not the first attempt): returned no merge blocker on the code and confirmed the read path by driving get_locale() against 12 adversarial cases - hostile stored values, junk rows, a translation removed from the image, Guest, anonymous OPDS. It found the proof apparatus wanting, not the fix: the guard blind spot above; the boundary having only source scans, which survive a BYPASS mutant (`coerce, then return the raw value`) even though they catch a deletion; and a trap where the account GET returned the raw stored locale, so a legacy bad row made the SPA language control display English while holding the bad string and 400 the entire next save - punishing exactly the users this fix rescues. All three fixed: an executing 8-case get_locale test (only the pt-BR normalisation case discriminates the bypass mutant), and the serializer now reports the EFFECTIVE locale via a fail-open helper. Performance measured rather than argued: the read-path coercion adds 5.337 us per authenticated request (200k calls, post-warm), 0.107%% of a 5 ms request; get_available_translations() was already called unconditionally before this change.
